mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, leading to higher valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 3% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and depressing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in high unemployment regimes (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE falls below 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above 1400 thousand units (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise and industrial production (INDPRO) falls simultaneously, it indicates a demand surge in housing but supply constraints in manufacturing, leading to inflationary pressures and negative equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST rises and INDPRO falls (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime, a fall in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced manufacturing output and potential inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls > 2.0pp in a supply shock regime (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
